### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **55** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-knowledge/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**38** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f77d078da5f88caf4615f45775172b49310c07c9`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-knowledge/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **15** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **186** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f77d078da5f88caf4615f45775172b49310c07c9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bfa2aca7907954e076c33556fe59e9f0f022eb9b` — the merge of head `ad74f6f069849c64cab87c1ad86006fc59b746e4` into base `f77d078da5f88caf4615f45775172b49310c07c9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bfa2aca7907954e076c33556fe59e9f0f022eb9b && git checkout bfa2aca7907954e076c33556fe59e9f0f022eb9b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f77d078da5f88caf4615f45775172b49310c07c9 ad74f6f069849c64cab87c1ad86006fc59b746e4 && git checkout -B drift-repro f77d078da5f88caf4615f45775172b49310c07c9 && git merge --no-ff ad74f6f069849c64cab87c1ad86006fc59b746e4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f77d078da5f88caf4615f45775172b49310c07c9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f77d078da5f88caf4615f45775172b49310c07c9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2c923172541d031c834aac4f9c4669c95b68c0f5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts + packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-tools.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/index.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts, packages/mcp/src/plugin.ts, packages/mcp/src/skill-prompts.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-ai-tool-references.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-file-tools.test.ts (the pin holding `MCP_DOOR_TOOL_NAMES` equal to what `wireBridgeTools` registers)
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

PR #36823 for card #36650. Inputs read: the card body and its four comments, the PR body, file list and net diff at this head, the check-runs on this head, and the live tree on `main` (4c18c43d) for the code the diff cites. The remainder of the diff (the four new or changed test files other than the pin above, the three `content/docs/**` pages, the changeset body) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `MCP_DOOR_TOOL_NAMES` gains `search_knowledge` (published constant in `@objectstack/spec/system`, value widened by one member, sorted position correct between `run_action` and `search_package_docs`). **Right.** The list's maintenance contract is "the exact set `wireBridgeTools` registers on a bridge carrying every optional member under every scope"; the diff adds `registerKnowledgeTools` to `wireBridgeTools` and adds both knowledge members to the full bridge of the conformance pin in `mcp-file-tools.test.ts`, so the two move together. Lint resolution is unchanged by the new member (`search_knowledge` already resolved through `PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE['service-ai']`); its one new effect is that the name is not in the diff's `ASK_TOOLS_THE_MCP_DOOR_LACKS` set, which is correct.
2. MCP tool surface: a new read-family tool on `tools/list`, on both transports, where the kernel holds a `knowledge` service carrying `knowledgeTools` and the grant is `data:read` or absent. **Right**, and a widening: every already-declared knowledge source whose `aiExposed` is unset becomes searchable by MCP clients on upgrade. That is the declared meaning of the default (`knowledge-source.zod.ts:159`, `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md:254`) and the changeset says it in its first paragraph.
3. `McpDataBridge` gains two OPTIONAL members (`searchKnowledge`, `knowledgeToolDefinitions`); `StdioDataBridgeDeps` gains optional `knowledgeTools`; `buildMcpBridge`'s `seams` gains optional `knowledgeTools`. **Right**: additive, absent means not registered, same degradation contract as the dataset pair.
4. `@objectstack/service-knowledge` publishes five values and five types from `knowledge-tools.ts`, and `KnowledgeService` gains the public method `knowledgeTools()`. **Right**: additive. `IKnowledgeService` (spec contract) is untouched, and both hosts detect the seam structurally, so a third-party knowledge service without the method serves no MCP tool rather than a broken one.
5. Accept set of the new tool: a closed object (`query`, `sourceIds`, `topK` 1..20), and a `sourceIds` entry that is not an exposed source is refused. **Right.** It is narrower than `IKnowledgeService.search`, but on a tool that did not exist: nothing published is narrowed, and `search()` itself is unchanged (read in the live tree: `resolveSearchTargets` still returns any registered source named explicitly).
6. `prompts/list` on the HTTP door now lists a skill binding `search_knowledge` where the tool is served. **Right**: a consequence of 2 through the unchanged `skillBindingServed`. `registerSkillPrompts` gains a third optional parameter: additive.
7. `ai-skill-tool-unresolved` gains a second verdict at warning severity for a projected skill binding `aggregate_data`, `query_data` or `visualize_data`. **Right as a firing set** (see ④, N1 for its wording): the accept set of `os validate` is unchanged, the rule stays advisory (ADR-0078), and `projectedOverMcp` mirrors `projectSkillPrompt` clause for clause (`active`, `mcpPrompt`, non-blank `instructions`). The verdict rides a rule id that says "unresolved" for a name that resolves; the explain text carries the distinction, so this is accepted as written.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, `mcp`, `runtime`, `spec`, `lint`. **Matches**: the five are exactly the released packages the diff moves; `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct (no key, accepted value or metadata type an author can write changes: `skill.tools` took the name before, and no Zod shape moves), and by AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 the kind `none` takes `patch` for a non-protocol widening. All five sit in the one `fixed` group, so they version together regardless. `Check Changeset` concluded `success` on this head.

Clause-②: yes — correct, and present line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset body. The diff enlarges the public surface (items 1 to 6 above) and narrows no published accept set, so no arm is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev report 7120236221, `open_questions`: empty.** Nothing to answer.
- **`out_of_scope_findings` 1** (a skill bound to a `stack.tools` record name is withheld by every MCP connection and the new verdict does not cover it; a binding served only where an optional service is mounted is covered by the debug line alone): confirmed by reading `bindingEntryServed` and the lint rule; a true gap that needs deployment knowledge authoring time lacks. Answered: accepted as stated, carrier none.
- **`out_of_scope_findings` 2** (cloud#4933 can register the open definition): the cloud repository is outside this review's inputs. NOT MEASURED here either; answered as a pointer for the cloud lane, no claim made.
- **`l2_routing`**: answered by this record. The tree decides the face: `packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts` is a published-schema path, so `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is owed and served.
- **Dev deviations**: branch not merged with the three `main` commits that landed after the branch point (none touch the changed paths; the merge queue re-tests on the merged tree); no dogfood battery (no `!`, no narrowing arm): both accepted.
- **`security_findings: none` — not accepted as written; escalated as E1.** `search_knowledge` is the first read on the MCP door that does not pass the door-level gates every other MCP read passes. The knowledge service re-checks each object-source hit by `dataEngine.find(object, { where: { id: { $in } }, fields: ['id'], context })`: that is row-level (and whatever object-level read the engine enforces) and nothing else. So a caller who may read a ROW receives passage text built from every `contentFields` member of it, including a field a field-level permission hides from that caller; and the object's MCP/API exposure posture (`enforceApiExposure` on stdio, the data door's on HTTP, including the disabled-package refusal) is never asked. This is the documented Phase-1 limit of the protocol (`content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx` §7.1 "Field-level masking — Phase 1 enforces row-level only", §9), it is exactly the gate the card's Expected item 1 names, and the author opts in per source through `contentFields` and `aiExposed`; so it is not graded against this diff. But this PR is what first puts that limit in front of end-user principals on the open distribution, and `packages/qa/dogfood/test/authz-conformance.matrix.ts:529` still states of the MCP door that "RLS / FLS / tenant apply exactly as on REST /data". **E1, for the maintainer through the seat:** decide whether the MCP knowledge tool keeps the protocol's row-level posture as is, or additionally drops a hit whose object fails the caller's exposure gate or whose content fields the caller cannot read; the seat files the decision card and names it in its ACCEPT. The PR body's 维护者速读 line holds at record level, not at field level, and should be read that way.
- **Observation, not graded (code outside the diff):** `KnowledgeService.search` logs and swallows an adapter failure and answers `[]`, so on a vector-store outage the tool answers "no hits" and its description tells the model to say nothing matched. The MCP door distinguishes outage from miss elsewhere (ADR-0110 D3); the executor cannot from what `search()` returns. Follow-up material for the knowledge service, not this head.
- **SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5):** no finding. The diff adds no id materialisation and no in-app join. The executor filters the in-memory source registry (`listSources()`), not rows. The one `id $in` read on the path is `applyPermissionFilter`, outside the diff and unchanged, and it has its reason: the ids come from the vector adapter's hits, which no SQL statement can join against.
- **Gate verdicts on this head** (check-runs read at record time): every completed run concluded `success` or `skipped` (among them `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Spec property liveness`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, Test Core shards 1 to 7, 9 and 10, all Test UI shards), except `Test Core (8/10)`: attempt 1 concluded `failure`, its rerun is `in_progress`, and the aggregate `Test Core` with it. I read attempt 1's log (job 138173799552): four failed tests, all timeouts, one in `@objectstack/plugin-audit` (`comment-reply-notice.integration.test.ts`, 5000 ms) and three in `@objectstack/plugin-security` (`delegated-organization-membership.test.ts` 5000 ms, `org-admin-assignment-boundary.posture.test.ts` 5000 ms and 9000 ms). Neither package is in the diff, and neither imports the changed modules beyond `@objectstack/spec`, whose only change is one string in a constant array. The brief described three 5000 ms timeouts; the log shows four tests, one of them at 9000 ms. This record does not stand in for that shard: the head is not all-green until the rerun concludes, and the seat's pre-landing check reads it.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts` (hits).** Holds. The new JSDoc clause says `search_knowledge` is served "where the kernel holds a `knowledge` service: the knowledge service's one definition and executor, searching only the sources whose `aiExposed` is not `false`, as the caller". Each part read against the code it describes: registration is conditional on both bridge members, which both hosts supply only when the kernel's `knowledge` service has `knowledgeTools` (`plugin.ts#knowledgeToolsService`, `runtime/domains/mcp.ts#resolveMcpKnowledgeToolsService`); the definition and executor are `knowledge-tools.ts`'s; the exposure filter and the context hand-off are in that executor. First consumer, the lint rule: unchanged resolution, correct exclusion from the withheld set. The scenario the card is accepted against (a skill with `tools: ['search_knowledge', 'query_records', 'get_record', 'action_…']` listed by `prompts/list`, and the source searchable): every entry is now served on an admin session with the knowledge service mounted, so `skillBindingServed` passes.

**Break attempts on the implementing files.**

- *Can an MCP caller reach an `aiExposed: false` source?* No. The only path from the door to the service is `knowledgeTools().searchKnowledge`. The executor builds `byId` from `listSources().filter(aiExposed !== false)`, refuses any `sourceIds` entry outside it before `search()` runs, always passes an explicit non-empty target list (so `resolveSearchTargets`' own implicit filter is not what is relied on), and filters returned hits by `byId` again. The refusal sentence is the same for an unknown and a withheld id and lists exposed ids only. On a stdio host whose AI registry also registers a `search_knowledge`, the native tool takes the name in either order (`bridgeTools` skip, `yieldBridgedTool`), so the open executor is the one served.
- *Is the caller's context what reaches the row-level re-check?* Yes on both transports. HTTP: `buildMcpBridge` closes over `ec = context.executionContext` and calls `searchKnowledge(input, ec)`; the executor forwards it as `executionContext`; `applyPermissionFilter` passes it to `dataEngine.find` as `context`. Stdio: `await resolvePrincipal()` per call, the same resolution the dataset pair uses. A missing context fails closed on object-source hits (read in the live tree).
- *Registered without `data:read`, or without a knowledge service?* No. `knowledgeToolDefinition` returns nothing for a grant lacking the scope or a bridge lacking either member, and the runtime does not resolve the service for such a grant at all.
- *ADR-0149 D2, one definition and one executor.* Holds in this repository: `packages/mcp` registers `definition.description` and `definition.parameters` as handed over and keeps only the name constant, tied by the conformance pin. It departs from D2's dataset precedent in one respect, accepted: the argument shape is hand-written JSON Schema in the service package with a hand-written `parseInput` beside it, where D2 put the dataset shapes in spec as zod projected to JSON Schema; and the output shape has no schema. Two descriptions of one accept set in one file is what S1 below falls out of.
- *Does the lint verdict fire correctly, and not on served tools?* The firing set is right for the HTTP door: `handleHttpRequest` never bridges the AI registry, so those three names are served there by nothing in this repository, and the dataset, docs and knowledge names are excluded by construction. See N1 for the claim's reach.
- `skill-prompts.ts`: moving projection ahead of the binding test changes no listing (a row that does not project was dropped either way) and limits the debug line to skills that would have been offered. `prompts/get` passes no reporter, so one listing logs once. Agrees with its JSDoc.

**Findings.**

S1 (should-fix) — `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-tools.ts`, `createKnowledgeTools`: a call with `sourceIds: []` searches nothing and answers `{ hits: [], sources }` with no refusal. `parseInput` accepts the empty array (the JSON Schema declares no `minItems`, so the door's converted schema admits it too), `if (sourceIds)` is true, `targets = sourceIds ?? [...]` is `[]`, and the `targets.length === 0` early return fires. The service the executor wraps treats the same input as "every exposed source" (`resolveSearchTargets`: `!sourceIds || sourceIds.length === 0`), and the tool's own description tells the model that no passage "means nothing the caller may read matched: say so rather than answer from general knowledge". An empty array for an optional list is a routine model output, and the card's acceptance scenario is a small BYO model answering policy questions from this tool: it would be told, falsely and silently, that the knowledge base has no basis. No pin covers the case (the new suite tests an unknown id, a withheld id and the all-withheld registry, not the empty list). Fix in the executor, one of: treat an empty `sourceIds` as omitted, as `search()` does; or declare `minItems: 1` and refuse the empty list `VALIDATION_ERROR`. Either way add the pin.

N1 (nit) — `packages/lint/src/validate-ai-tool-references.ts` and `rule-explanations.ts`: the verdict says the tool is served "by no MCP connection" and that MCP withholds the skill from `prompts/list`. That is the HTTP door. The long-lived stdio server bridges the host's AI registry (`plugin.ts:449-451`, `MCPServerRuntime.bridgeTools`), so on a host whose `ai` service registers those tools a stdio connection lists them, and stdio registers skill prompts without the binding filter (the PR body's own acceptance note). Every stack the verdict fires on is withheld on the HTTP door, so the firing set stands; only the sentence over-reaches. Left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up that says "the HTTP door".

N2 (nit) — `knowledge-tools.ts` module JSDoc states as present fact that "an in-product registry registers the same definition and delegates to the same executor". Nothing in this review's inputs shows that, and the card records cloud#4933 as not registering the tool at all. The sentence describes the intended shape. Accepted deviation.

N3 (nit) — `mcp-http-tools.ts#knowledgeToolDefinition` calls itself "the one gate" while `registerKnowledgeTools` has a second way to register nothing (a definition that does not convert to an object schema). No caller reads the former as a served-predicate today, so nothing disagrees yet. Accepted deviation.

One should-fix (S1), no must-fix. S1 earns a delta review of its fix on the head that carries it; E1 goes to the maintainer through the seat and does not wait on that delta.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-36650-mcp-search-knowledge`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYpEsWWE9Y5YtSsDgqZ`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ad74f6f069849c64cab87c1ad86006fc59b746e4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts + packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-tools.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/index.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts, packages/mcp/src/plugin.ts, packages/mcp/src/skill-prompts.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-ai-tool-references.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-file-tools.test.ts (the pin holding `MCP_DOOR_TOOL_NAMES` equal to what `wireBridgeTools` registers)
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

Delta review of PR #36823 (card #36650) after the record on head `2c923172541d031c834aac4f9c4669c95b68c0f5`. Inputs read: the compare `2c923172…ad74f6f0` (status `ahead`, 2 commits, 0 behind: `f4b486c4f1` and `ad74f6f069`, each one parent, no merge), the dev's rework report 7120914341 on the card, the PR body as patched, and the check-runs on the new head. The first record's ①, ② and ④ stand for every file this delta does not move; only what moved is re-judged here.

What moved, whole: `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-tools.ts` (+12 −1, the one implementing file), two test files (`service-knowledge/src/__tests__/knowledge-tools.test.ts` +4 −1, `mcp/src/mcp-knowledge-tools.test.ts` +10 −1), and the changeset body (+1 −1, prose). The `hits` file and the eleven other implementing files are byte-identical to the reviewed head: none appears in the compare's file list.

### ① Derived judgments

One change to the first record's item 5. The tool's argument accept set narrows by one value: `sourceIds: []` is now refused, by the definition (`minItems: 1`) and by the executor (`VALIDATION_ERROR`, 400). **Right.** The tool is unreleased, so no published accept set narrows and no `(narrowing)` arm is owed; `IKnowledgeService.search` is untouched and still reads an empty list as every exposed source. Items 1 to 4, 6 and 7 are unchanged.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `patch` on the same five packages, `Metadata-protocol: none`. The delta moves no package the changeset does not already name.

Clause-②: yes — still correct, and still line-initial in the PR body and the changeset body. The changeset's argument sentence now states the refusal, which matches the code.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Rework report 7120914341, `open_questions`: empty.** Its one deviation (the spec, lint and runtime suites were not re-run locally because the delta does not touch those packages) is accepted: CI runs them on this head.
- **Its `security_findings: none`** is answered as before: E1 from the first record is untouched by this delta and stays with the maintainer through the seat. It does not wait on this record and this record does not close it.
- **SQL push-down:** no finding. The delta adds one length check on an argument; no read, no id materialisation, no join.
- **Gate verdicts on this head, read at record time:** 12 check-runs concluded `success`, 11 `skipped`, and 18 were still `in_progress`, among them `Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, the `Lint ·` families, the four `Type Check ·` jobs and the two shard planners; no Test Core or Test UI shard had been created yet. None had failed. This record stands in for none of them: the two new pins and the definition pin are proven only when the shards that carry `@objectstack/service-knowledge` and `@objectstack/mcp` conclude, and the seat's pre-landing check reads the full set.

### ④ Design judgment

**S1: closed.** Read in `knowledge-tools.ts` at this head: `SEARCH_KNOWLEDGE_PARAMETERS.sourceIds` declares `minItems: 1`, and `parseInput` throws `VALIDATION_ERROR`/400 when `record.sourceIds.length === 0`, placed after the array-and-entries check and before the dedupe, so no empty list reaches `createKnowledgeTools`. The refusal sentence names both ways out (omit it, or name at least one listed id), which is what a model needs to correct the call.
